article_title: Exploring the impact of phonological awareness, visual–spatial working memory, and preschool quantity–number competencies on mathematics achievement in elementary school: Findings from a 3-year longitudinal study
citation: Krajewski, K., & Schneider, W. (2009). Exploring the impact of phonological awareness, visual-spatial working memory, and preschool quantity-number competencies on mathematics achievement in elementary school: Findings from a 3-year longitudinal study. Journal of Experimental Child Psychology, 103(4), 516-531. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jecp.2009.03.009
title: Krajewski's three-level developmental model of quantity-number competencies (QNC)
description: A theoretical model of early arithmetical development describing how mathematical competencies are acquired via three developmental levels of quantity-to-number-word linkage. At Level I children recite number words with the words still isolated from quantities; at Level II (imprecise then precise) children understand that number words are linked to quantities and can arrange numbers by size; at Level III children understand part-whole relations and differences between numbers represented with precise number words. The study used this model to derive differential predictions for phonological awareness and visual-spatial working memory, quoting that it "depicts how this linkage might occur and how early mathematical competencies are acquired via three developmental levels".
requirements: Assessment tasks distinguishing number-word sequence knowledge (Level I) from quantity-to-number-word linkage (Level II) and number relations (Level III)
constraints: The authors note the model's level differentiation was necessary to detect the differential predictor effects; studies not differentiating QNC levels found inconsistent phonological-awareness effects
target_learning_goals: understanding of the number system and quantity-to-number-word linkage
examples: The study operationalized the levels with tasks such as number-word sequence recitation (Level I), quantity-comparison and number-word comparison tasks (Level II), and difference and word problems with concrete material (Level III)
